acceptance: The cause of the TempDir cleanup failure is measured and named: the process or file that still writes under the fixture git repo when t.TempDir cleanup runs
A red test or a stress run reproduces it before the fix: go test -count=200 -run '^TestDocDelete_' ./internal/guards/ under load, or a direct proof of the leftover writer
After the fix the same stress run passes, and the fixture uses internal/gittest
The change touches only test files of go/internal/guards and, when needed, go/internal/gittest
fix: Cycle 2494 build round 1 (2026-11-18 05:46 UTC, .evolve/runs/cycle-2494/build-interactions.ndjson kind salvage) failed the repo-contract scanner pack on guards.TestDocDelete_EverythingElseUnderTheDocRootsStaysProtected with 'testing.go:1619: TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat <tmp>/TestDocDelete_...'. The test passes on main (go test -count=1, 0.4 s). The fixture laneWithADraft (docdelete_uncommitted_test.go:57) builds a git repo in t.TempDir and the guard runs git in it, so a git child or lock file that outlives the test is the first hypothesis. The flake had a cost: the host proved the cycle's protected-path blocker but refused to end the cycle because this failure was not explained, so the cycle ran two more repair rounds (see repair-fixability-stop-flip-to-enforce-after-cycle-2494). Record the issue through the issue-record skill.
